builder_plan.scenario: A self-hosted model uses more compute or memory than your workload can justify.
builder_plan.change: Check for a usable pruned checkpoint and runtime support before attempting model surgery.
builder_plan.baseline: The original unpruned model at the same precision, context, and load.
steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.
builder_plan.measure: Task quality, actual GPU memory, serving throughput, and preparation cost.
builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: CRISP: Co-designing Pruning and Scheduling for Efficient MoE Inference on Edge Servers
summary: The technique replaces uniform expert pruning and naive expert dropping with a combination-aware framework that co-designs neuron-level importance pruning and runtime scheduling of expert execution widths. The cost is a static accuracy loss of up to 3.6% relative to the full model and the complexity of implementing a specialized runtime scheduler for hot, warm, and cold expert combinations. The method could fail if real-world query distributions do not exhibit the same skewed expert combination frequencies found in the paper's benchmarks, reducing the effectiveness of the differentiated scheduling.
rationale: This method is specific to serving Mixture-of-Experts models on memory-constrained edge servers, which does not align with the reader's single 24GB GPU or API-based infrastructure and requires implementing a custom runtime scheduler.
technique: Combination-aware pruning and scheduling for MoE edge inference

claims.statement: The technique replaces uniform expert pruning and naive expert dropping with a combination-aware framework that co-designs neuron-level importance pruning and runtime scheduling of expert execution widths. The cost is a static accuracy loss of up to 3.6% relative to the full model and the complexity of implementing a specialized runtime scheduler for hot, warm, and cold expert combinations. The method could fail if real-world query distributions do not exhibit the same skewed expert combination frequencies found in the paper's benchmarks, reducing the effectiveness of the differentiated scheduling.
CRISP improves throughput by up to 2.1x at the same memory budget while limiting accuracy loss to 3.6% relative to full-width inference.
